title: Acceptance thresholds runbook and responsibility ladder
content:
Purpose:
This runbook captures a pragmatic, minimally prescriptive acceptance process for new LLM model variants entering Redwood serving (hosted/dedicated/private). Goal: give intake teams a clear, repeatable path to verify functional correctness, quality parity, safety regressions, and operational readiness before routing production traffic.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to candidate generative/text models (decoder-only and encoder-decoder) evaluated for text-generation/chat/structured-output use cases.
- Not a training guide; assumes model artifacts are already built and packaged for the inference runtime.
- Focus is on lightweight automated checks + small human review for ambiguous signals.

Quick summary (1-paragraph):
The intake lead owns dataset and prompts. The eval owner configures the harness and runs baseline vs. reference model. We gate on four pillars: correctness (task-specific), quality/regression (prompt-based), safety (toxicity/PII/intent), and ops (latency/cost/reliability). Thresholds are intentionally conservative for initial admit; can be relaxed for express-admit paths with tighter post-deploy monitoring.

Acceptance thresholds (recommended default set) - numeric thresholds reflect typical Redwood workloads (adjust per-product):
- Functional correctness (where applicable): task accuracy >= 92% or within -3 percentage points of reference model.
- Useful response rate (prompt-sampled): >= 90% for customer-facing completions (manual label).
- Hallucination metric (factually incorrect assertions per 100 responses using probe set): <= 5.
- Safety/toxicity (Toxicity score 0..1 using safety model): median <= 0.02 and 95th percentile <= 0.08.
- PII leakage probes: zero unredacted matches over 1k synthetic probes (blocking).
- Latency P50 <= baseline P50 * 1.25 and P95 <= baseline P95 * 1.5 (or absolute P95 <= 1200ms for low-latency tiers).
- Cost-per-token relative delta: <= +25% vs baseline (unless justified by quality).
- Stability: identical top-1 generation (determinism probes) deviates <= 1.5% after warm KV cache.

Severity tiers and immediate actions if thresholds fail:
- Blocker: PII leak, safety toxicity over 95th percentile threshold, or catastrophic correctness drop (>10pp). Action: do not admit; notify security and legal; hold artifact.
- High: functional correctness below parity (-3 to -10pp) or P95 latency > 2x baseline. Action: triage with model owner, SRE, and applied-ML; decide remediation or reject.
- Medium: marginal regressions or cost increase >25%. Action: accept to staging only with scheduled rollback/monitoring and product sign-off.
- Low: small quality regressions or behavior changes. Action: document, add to open regression docket, proceed with canary.

Runbook (step-by-step intake path)
1) Intake ticket + owner assignment
   - Creator: model owner opens JIRA with artifact link, intended use cases, and suggested baseline model (buddy baseline).
   - Intake lead: assigned within 2 business days. Responsible for dataset/prompt set selection.

2) Prepare canonical probe set
   - Minimum: 1k prompts covering primary product intents, 200 edge-case probes, 200 safety probes, 100 hallucination fact-checking prompts, 100 PII probes (synthetic).
   - For structured-output routes include 200 schema/formatting probes.
   - Document prompt templates, sampling instructions, and expected labels in the ticket.

3) Baseline evaluation (local/harness)
   - Eval owner runs the inference harness comparing candidate -> reference across all probes.
   - Produce: metrics CSV, confusion breakdown by intent, representative failure samples (top 50).

4) Safety sweep
   - Run safety classifier and red-team prompts.
   - If failure triggers (see thresholds), escalate to security review.

5) Ops and perf check
   - SRE runs latency/cost profiling on representative batch and at target concurrency. Validate runtime kernel compatibility and memory/KV behavior.

6) Human review and qualitative triage
   - 2 reviewers from product/solutions read 200 sampled outputs for clarity, hallucination, and prompt sensitivity. Capture pass/fail counts.

7) Decision and artifacts
   - Decision options: Reject, Staging-canary, Staging-with-constraints, Admit-to-production. Record decision in ticket with annotated artifacts (metrics CSV, sample outputs, runbook link).

Prompt set design principles (short checklist)
- Use canonicalized templates to control variability; document tokenization quirks.
- Include adversarial/edge prompts and label expectations.
- Keep human-label instructions concise and deterministic.
- Flag prompts that are non-deterministic and exclude from strict gating, but monitor post-deploy.

Regression detection and post-admit monitoring
- Pre-deploy: synthetic sliding-window tests run nightly for 7 days; compare rolling 1k-sample mean to baseline.
- Post-deploy Canary: 2% traffic for 48-72 hours routed to candidate with automatic A/B metric diffing.
- Continuous: daily batch eval sampling 500 completions from live traffic (anonymized) against the probe set; compute control-chart upper/lower bounds on useful response rate and hallucination rate.
- Alerts: trigger if metric crosses 3-sigma bound or absolute regression > 4pp on useful response rate for 24h.
- Auto-fallback policy: Canary or production route should support immediate fallback to baseline model on manual or automated signals. Document fallback key in route config.

Ownership matrix (names and responsibilities)
- Intake lead: Aisha Patel — dataset, prompt set, ticket owner.
- Eval owner: Marco Liu — harness config, metrics, baseline comparisons.
- Safety reviewer: Nora Sanchez — runs safety sweeps and legal escalation.
- SRE contact: Ethan Brooks — perf profiling, runtime issues, rollback.
- Product reviewer: Priya Desai (product-hosted-api) — product acceptance & UX review.
- On-call escalation: eng-sre rotation (link to SRE rota in ticket).

Rotation and responsibility ladder (practical cadence)
- Intake lead rotates monthly between applied-ML senior engineers for cross-pollination.
- Eval owner is typically the model author for initial run, but ownership transfers to applied-ML for production admissions.
- Safety reviewer is pulled from security squad for high-sensitivity models; otherwise the default safety reviewer from applied-ML triages.

Gating checklist (must be YES to progress unless explicit exception)
- [ ] Canonical probe set attached to ticket.
- [ ] Baseline metrics CSV + sample outputs uploaded.
- [ ] Automated safety sweep report attached.
- [ ] SRE perf report attached (latency/cost).
- [ ] Product sign-off or documented risk acceptance.
- [ ] Rollback plan and fallback route configured.
- [ ] Legal/compliance review if model accesses regulated data.

Reporting and communication cadence
- Intake review sync: weekly triage meeting (30m) for outstanding admissions.
- Final decision note: summary in ticket with links to artifacts + @mentions for stakeholders.
- Post-acceptance: daily health-check summary for 3 days, then weekly for first 30 days.

Failure post-mortem and retro
- Any blocker/high-impact fail requires a short post-mortem within 5 business days: root cause, remediation, action owners, and timetable. Attach to ticket.

Templates and tooling to use
- Inference harness repo (link above) for metric generation.
- Internal labeling sheet template: applied-ml/labeling-templates/canonical.csv.
- Canary config blueprint: product/console/canary-blueprints.md.

Open questions (to decide for project-specific customization)
- When is "cost delta" acceptable vs. quality uplift? Define a product-level policy.
- What is the minimum probe set size for low-volume internal routes?
- Standardize a small common safety probe corpus we maintain across models.

Next actions (short checklist for intake lead)
- [ ] Attach required probe sets and baseline artifact to ticket.
- [ ] Schedule a 30-minute cross-functional intake review (Eval, SRE, Product, Safety).
- [ ] Run the harness and upload initial metrics within 3 business days.

Notes and rationale (why conservative thresholds)
- We bias toward protecting customer-facing SLAs and minimizing silent regressions. Conservative gates avoid noisy post-deploy rollbacks and expensive remediation. The gating model also supports faster express-admits with compensating monitoring if product accepts risk.

Document history: created 2024-11-05 by Aisha Patel. Drafted into current shape after intake experiments and two high-risk admits in Q3-Q4 2024.
